chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAzramī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I prayed behind Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام over a جنازة, and he said the takbir five times, raising his hands with each takbir.

key_terms.جِنَازَةٍ: funeral bier or deceased person over whom the funeral prayer is performed
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five times, referring to the number of takbirs
key_terms.كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَةٍ: each individual takbir in the prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended to raise the hands in every takbir of the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in the funeral prayer. It indicates that five takbirs were said over the جنازة and that he raised his hands with each takbir, making it evidence for a jurisprudential ruling in salat over the deceased.
